summary: Clarity for Compensation Act This bill allows individuals who work for registered brokers to receive compensation for their services through their own personal businesses without having to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).  Specifically, the bill exempts certain personal services entities from SEC broker regulations. As background, brokers (persons engaged in the business of making securities transactions on behalf of others) must register with the SEC and become members of a self-regulatory organization (SRO). Under this bill, a  personal services entity is an entity established by a registered representative to receive compensation for services from the registered representative's broker.
